title: Persona — The Embodied WebMCP AI Agent
pitch: Persona gives AI agents a body—letting them understand your intent, act through WebMCP, and respond naturally with voice, gaze, expressions, and gestures. Making every interaction feel human.

 Inspiration 

 We are at a strange point in the evolution of AI. 

 AI can reason, write code, analyze information, use tools, and increasingly perform tasks on our behalf. But when it comes time to actually interact with it, we are still mostly staring at a text box. 

 Type a prompt.
Wait.
Read a long response.
Type again. 

 It works, but it can feel surprisingly disconnected. 

 I kept thinking about a simple question: 

 
 If AI is becoming capable of doing things like a person, why are we still interacting with it like a search box? 
 

 Humans don't communicate through words alone. 

 We use our voice. We look at each other. We react. We gesture. We pay attention. We pause. We interrupt. We change our expression when something is important. 

 Those small signals make communication easier to understand. 

 So we wanted to explore a different kind of AI interface. 

 
 What if an AI agent had a body? 
 

 That question became Persona . 

 The goal wasn't to create a character that simply talks to you or to make AI pretend to be human. 

 The goal was to explore whether an AI agent could have a presence — a way to communicate its intent through voice, attention, expressions, gestures, and visible actions while still doing useful work. 

 WebMCP made this idea especially interesting. 

 Instead of an AI agent trying to figure out which button to click or how a webpage happens to be structured, the webpage can explicitly expose capabilities that the agent can discover and use. 

 That gave us an opportunity to build something where the agent doesn't just talk about what it wants to do. 

 It can actually interact with the webpage through structured tools. 

 And if an agent can control actions on the web, why shouldn't it also be able to control how it communicates with the person standing on the other side of the interaction? 

 That became the idea behind Persona: 

 
 Give the agent a body. Give that body meaningful capabilities. Then let WebMCP connect the agent to them. 
 

 

 What it does 

 Persona is an embodied WebMCP AI agent interface. 

 It gives an AI agent a digital body that can listen, speak, look, react, gesture, and perform structured tasks . 

 Instead of treating the avatar as a visual layer placed on top of a chatbot, Persona makes the avatar part of the agent interaction itself. 

 A user can communicate naturally through voice, while an AI agent can discover and call WebMCP tools exposed by Persona. 

 The agent can: 

 
 Understand the user's spoken intent 
 Create tasks and missions 
 Read the current task state 
 Update tasks when requirements change 
 Complete tasks 
 Present results 
 Speak to the user 
 Change its expression 
 Direct its attention and gaze 
 Perform gestures 
 

 The WebMCP tools exposed by Persona include: 
 get_user_transcript
create_task
get_tasks
update_task
complete_task
show_result
speak
set_expression
set_attention
perform_gesture
 
 This allows the agent to interact with two sides of the application: 

 What it is doing and how it is communicating while doing it . 

 For example, a user can say: 

 
 "Prepare me for a data science technical interview tomorrow." 
 

 The agent can turn that request into a structured mission instead of simply returning a large block of advice. 

 The user can then change their mind: 

 
 "Actually, focus much more on machine learning." 
 

 The agent can update the mission and continue from the current state. 

 At the same time, Persona can communicate through speech, attention, expressions, and gestures. 

 This creates an interaction loop where: 

 Human intent → Agent reasoning → WebMCP action → Application state → Embodied response 

 The interview-preparation scenario is our concrete demonstration of this idea. 

 But Persona itself isn't meant to be just an interview coach. 

 The larger idea is an embodied interface for web agents . 

 The avatar is not there just to look good. 

 The agent can actually control it through WebMCP. 

 That is what turns Persona from an animated chatbot into an exploration of what an agent-native web interface could look and feel like. 

 

 How we built it 

 Persona is a browser-based application built with: 

 
 React 
 TypeScript 
 Vite 
 Three.js 
 VRM 
 @pixiv/three-vrm 
 WebMCP 
 Web Speech API 
 Web Audio API 
 

 The project combines an agent-facing tool layer with an embodiment runtime. 

 WebMCP tool layer 

 The core of the WebMCP integration is the application's ability to expose structured capabilities through document.modelContext . 

 Instead of exposing arbitrary UI elements, Persona exposes tools that represent meaningful actions an agent can perform. 

 For example: 
 document . modelContext . registerTool ( . . . ) 
 
 The tools cover two main areas. 

 Agent actions 
 create_task
get_tasks
update_task
complete_task
show_result
 
 These allow the agent to work with structured application state. 

 Embodiment actions 
 get_user_transcript
speak
set_expression
set_attention
perform_gesture
 
 These allow the agent to communicate through Persona's digital body. 

 This separation was important to us. 

 The AI agent doesn't need to know how the avatar is implemented internally. 

 It doesn't need to manipulate Three.js objects, animation clips, or VRM parameters. 

 It can simply use a meaningful capability such as: 
 speak(...)
set_expression(...)
set_attention(...)
perform_gesture(...)
 
 Persona handles the underlying implementation. 

 The embodiment runtime 

 The visual body is a VRM character rendered through Three.js. 

 Around that character, we built systems for: 

 
 Voice input 
 Voice output 
 Speech-driven mouth movement 
 Facial expressi

live_observation.first_impression: A dark dashboard presents Persona as an embodied WebMCP agent with selectable coaching personas, a tool registry, and agent activity areas. The technical interview persona is active.
